statements.title: Pre and Post Repair Scanning Requirements
statements.summary: All Honda/Acura vehicles (1996+) involved in a collision REQUIRE both pre-repair and post-repair diagnostic scans. Dashboard indicators are NOT acceptable for determining if scans are necessary.
statements.fullText: American Honda's position states that all vehicles involved in a collision (defined as damage that exceeds minor outer panel cosmetic distortion) must have minimum diagnostic scans, inspections and/or calibrations done to avoid improper repair. A pre-repair scan during estimation identifies DTCs present. A post-repair scan confirms no DTCs remain. Any repair requiring disconnection of electrical components requires a post-repair scan. Dashboard indicators are intended for driver notification, not vehicle diagnostics.
keyPoints: Pre-repair scan REQUIRED during estimation phase
Post-repair scan REQUIRED after all repairs complete
Applies to ALL 1996+ Honda/Acura vehicles
Dashboard warning lights are NOT sufficient - scan required regardless
Use i-HDS with 'All DTC Check' feature recommended

statements.fullText: Toyota recommends that a health check be performed prior to and after any collision repair to ensure all electronic systems are operating as designed. This includes vehicles that may not have visible damage to components containing electronic control units. Access to TIS repair manuals and technical bulletins is available at techinfo.toyota.com. ADAS information is found in Audio/Visual/Telematics, Engine/Hybrid System, Vehicle Interior, and ADAS/AD categories.
keyPoints: Health check BEFORE and AFTER collision repair strongly recommended

statements.title: Pre and Post-Scan of Collision Vehicles

Many safety and security-related components require calibration when replaced. MDI2 is required for 2021+ vehicles.

statements.title: Corrosion Protection Restoration
statements.summary: OEMs require restoring corrosion protection (weld-through primer, seam sealer, cavity wax) in the correct sequence. Per I-CAR: applying it at the wrong step 'can cause refinish defects and fire hazards' - always refer to the body repair manual.
statements.fullText: Per I-CAR RTS ('When to Apply Corrosion Protection During the Repair Process'): adhesives are applied before welding when bonding; foam fillers before refinish; seam sealers before or after refinishing per product; cavity wax after refinish but before trim. Applying corrosion protection at the wrong step can cause refinish defects and fire hazards (it cites a rocker-panel explosion from propellant fumes ignited during welding). Always refer to the body repair manual. Several OEMs specify zinc-based (not copper) weld-through primer.

statements.title: Aluminum-Intensive Repair Requirements
statements.summary: Aluminum-intensive repairs require an isolated work area and dedicated, aluminum-only tools to prevent galvanic corrosion and thermite-reaction risk. Some OEMs require a dedicated room; others allow a curtained bay. (Verified via ASA/AutoInc and BodyShopBusiness; documented programs: Ford F-150, Audi.)
statements.fullText: Industry sources (ASA/AutoInc. and BodyShopBusiness) confirm the requirement: some OEMs require dealers/approved shops to devote a room solely to aluminum repairs; others allow a curtain system to isolate a bay. Tools and equipment used on aluminum should not be shared with steel-vehicle tools and should be stored separately to prevent contamination (galvanic corrosion when steel dust contacts bare aluminum; thermite-reaction risk from mixed aluminum/steel dust, requiring separate vacuums). The best-documented OEM programs are Ford F-150 (aluminum clean-room + dedicated tooling) and Audi (dedicated aluminum tooling).
keyPoints: Isolated room or curtained bay for aluminum repair
Dedicated aluminum-only tools, stored separately
Prevents galvanic corrosion and thermite/fire risk
Separate vacuum/extraction required
Documented programs: Ford F-150, Audi

statements.title: Rivet-Bonding & Structural Adhesive
statements.summary: Per Ford's statement: aluminum vehicles require OEM structural repair rivets and approved installation tools; aftermarket structural rivets (self-piercing, blind, solid) are NOT authorized. These vehicles use mechanical fasteners and structural adhesive in place of spot welds; rivet placement cannot deviate from OEM procedures.
statements.fullText: Ford's 'Use of Non-OEM Structural Rivets' position statement (May 20, 2022) states all Ford vehicles with aluminum structural/cosmetic components require OEM structural repair rivets and approved installation tools, and that aftermarket structural rivets - including self-piercing (SPR), blind, and solid rivets - are not authorized. These vehicles use mechanical fasteners and structural adhesives (SPR, blind rivets, solid rivets, flow-drill screws) in place of conventional spot welds; rivets are not universal and placement cannot deviate from OEM procedures, and flow-drill screws cannot be reused. Ford lists the only approved SPR installation systems (Henrob, Pro Spot, Car-O-Liner PNP90, Chief, Spanesi, TKR, Wielander & Schill).
keyPoints: OEM structural rivets and approved tools required
Aftermarket SPR/blind/solid rivets NOT authorized
Fasteners + adhesive replace spot welds on aluminum
Rivet placement cannot deviate from OEM procedure
Flow-drill screws cannot be reused

statements.title: Wheel Alignment & Calibration Triggers
statements.summary: Per I-CAR: numerous OEMs require ADAS to be calibrated when a wheel alignment is performed. If the steering angle sensor is adjusted during an alignment, the forward-facing camera may misread steering position and cause incorrect corrections.
statements.fullText: Per I-CAR RTS ('The Effects of Wheel Alignment on ADAS'): if the steering angle sensor is adjusted during a wheel alignment, the forward-facing camera controlling lane departure may think the steering wheel is turned, causing incorrect steering corrections. Numerous OEMs require the ADAS to be calibrated when a wheel alignment is performed; refer to OEM repair information for the specific requirements and sequence. Related I-CAR guidance covers steering-angle/position-sensor calibration.
keyPoints: Numerous OEMs require ADAS calibration with wheel alignment
Steering-angle-sensor changes affect the forward camera
Misread steering angle can cause wrong corrections
Steering-angle-sensor calibration often required
Follow the OEM procedure for specific triggers

statements.title: Diagnostic Tool Selection (OEM vs Aftermarket)
statements.summary: Per Honda's position: the only way to accurately determine post-collision status of all Honda/Acura electronic systems is with factory-authorized i-HDS software; 'American Honda does not test other scan tools or remote diagnostic services and cannot comment on their capabilities or accuracy.'
statements.fullText: American Honda's position ('Post-Collision Diagnostic Scan and Calibration Requirements,' May 2019, v4) states the only way to accurately determine the post-collision status of all Honda/Acura electronic control systems is with the factory-authorized diagnostic software i-HDS, whose 'All DTC Check' scans every equipped ECU. It states American Honda does not test other scan tools or remote diagnostic services and cannot comment on their accuracy. Not all systems are accessible via i-HDS (e.g., LaneWatch), and many ADAS DTCs won't display unless the specific system is damaged. Stellantis and Ford also publish scan-tool/scan statements; Toyota advises verifying an aftermarket tool can retrieve History/Pending/Current DTCs.
keyPoints: Honda requires factory i-HDS for a complete scan
Honda does not validate other scan tools' accuracy
Not all aftermarket tools read all modules/DTCs
Some systems not accessible even via i-HDS
Stellantis/Ford have scan statements; verify tool capability
